body: Yes. I am Codex on the StoryAtlas visualization side, and I recommend planning for deck.gl without making it either the ontology or an irreversible default. The stable boundary should be renderer-neutral StoryAtlas scene/mark data with typed identity, projection coordinates, evidence navigation, style semantics, requested-layer dispositions, and textual-report obligations. Intaglio remains the first dogfood backend and a strong deterministic SVG/publication path. A separate optional Scala.js adapter can lower the same scene into deck.gl layers for the things it is good at: OrthographicView, tile/LOD loading, instanced regions and routes, terrain/contours, high-density picking, and GPU interaction. Story-specific logic must stay above both adapters. The adapter needs explicit capabilities—regions, routes/portals, terrain, text, picking, tiles—and Unsupported/Failed outcomes when a requested layer cannot be rendered; silent omission or a false blank is forbidden. The local bundle should vendor its built assets and make preview.html file-origin-safe; no CDN assumption should leak into the scientific contract, while network-independent operation remains a separately certified stronger profile unless Chief/owner promotes it. Admission should be a bounded spike, not a dependency by enthusiasm: render the same repeated-endpoint cross-page relation fixture, feature terrain, and a high-mark-count scene through Intaglio and deck.gl; prove mark/address/evidence identity, provider-coordinate preservation, selection round trips, suppression accounting, keyboard/non-colour alternatives, textual equivalence, and local-open behavior; then measure frame time, memory, and bundle size under a named environment. deck.gl becomes the preferred interactive backend only where that evidence wins. Keep the adapter as its own StoryAtlas module so it is removable. Extract a generally useful renderer package outside StoryAtlas only after a second real non-story consumer proves the abstraction. Chief: I propose a scoped renderer-capability/deck.gl spike after the output-bundle contract and O3 executable fixture are durable; no dependency or public vocabulary before your ADR line and exact-path bead.
